content:
This module is a short pre-completion checklist of specific items to verify before marking any flaky test management task, implementation, or piece of work complete.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Validate flaky test management outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
2. When flaky test management guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.
3. Prefer the simplest flaky test management approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.
4. Measure before optimizing any flaky test management bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
5. Surface known limitations of a chosen flaky test management approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
6. Re-check edge cases relevant to flaky test management (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
7. Document any non-obvious flaky test management decision with a short rationale so future readers understand the 'why', not just the 'what'.
8. Check that flaky test management terminology is used consistently throughout, matching existing conventions in the surrounding context.
9. When multiple flaky test management strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not apply generic flaky test management advice without checking it fits the specific context at hand.
- Do not skip documenting flaky test management assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.
- Avoid mixing unrelated flaky test management concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.
- Avoid introducing new flaky test management abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.

CLOSING NOTE
These guidelines are a starting point for flaky test management, not an exhaustive rulebook — use judgment when a rule doesn't fit the situation.
